draft.title: Chronic muscular adaptations
card: Chronic adaptations are lasting changes from weeks and months of regular training. Resistance training, such as lifting weights, changes the muscles and the nerves that control them.
an increase in the size of muscle fibres. Larger fibres can produce more force, so the muscle becomes stronger.
better control of muscle by the nerves. More fibres are recruited at once and they fire in a more coordinated way.
Early strength gains in a new program often come mostly from neural adaptation. Hypertrophy takes longer to build up.
draft.remember: Resistance training grows the fibres and trains the nerves to use them better.

opts: Nerves recruit more fibres at once
Muscle fibres split into new fibres
a.why: Hypertrophy is an increase in the size of muscle fibres. Recruiting more fibres is a neural adaptation, which is the tempting wrong option because it also raises strength.
a.clue: Hypertrophy is about size, not nerve control.

b.q: Priya starts a weights program in Geelong. After three weeks she can lift more, but her muscles look no bigger. What best explains this?
opts: Neural adaptation, as her nerves recruit fibres better
Hypertrophy, as her fibres have grown larger
A fall in force from her muscles
Her muscles have lost fibres to gain strength
b.why: Early strength gains often come mostly from neural adaptation, where the nerves recruit and coordinate more fibres. Hypertrophy is tempting because it also raises strength, but it takes longer and would show as bigger muscles.
b.clue: Strength rose but size did not.

b.best: Neural adaptation, as her nerves recruit fibres better
